claims.text: The proposed thermal–mechanical treatment will refine the alloy into a nanocrystalline microstructure.
The proposed treatment will induce slight enrichment of selected oxidation-promoting elements at grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary-enriched elements can form stable protective oxide scales.
Engineered lattice distortion together with nanoscale grain-boundary segregation lowers alloy density.
Engineered lattice distortion together with nanoscale grain-boundary segregation increases mechanical strength.
Engineered lattice distortion together with nanoscale grain-boundary segregation enhances corrosion resistance.
Engineered lattice distortion together with nanoscale grain-boundary segregation enhances high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Enhanced lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion and thereby increases strength.
Fine grains and selected grain-boundary segregation facilitate formation of adherent protective oxide layers.
Fine grains and selected grain-boundary segregation promote more uniform passive films.
The protective oxide layers improve oxidation resistance.
More uniform passive films improve corrosion resistance.
The proposed microstructural changes preserve the alloy's low density.
The processed alloy will have higher yield strength or nanoindentation hardness than the same-composition baseline.
The processed alloy will develop a thinner oxidation scale than the baseline.
The processed alloy's oxidation scale will adhere better than that of the baseline.
The processed alloy will have a lower corrosion rate than the baseline.
Above approximately 1100°C, engineered grain boundaries will become unstable, rapid grain coarsening will occur, and the proposed benefits will diminish.
Extremely aggressive oxidizing or corrosive environments can overwhelm the protective oxide or passive film and eliminate the proposed benefits.
